policy: included quota prorates by calendar day (quota * day_of_month / days_in_month, rounded UP to the next whole unit); first 25 overage units per month are a free grace allowance applied BEFORE block rounding; the remainder bills in 50-unit blocks rounded UP (partial block = full block) at plan['block_fee'] per block, never per unit
bug_report: Two customers escalated this week: one was charged mid-month while still under their plan quota, and another's tiny overage got billed the same as a much larger one - support keeps issuing manual credits and they're eating margin. A failing repro is at tests/test_regression.py. Fix overage_charge so invoices follow the metering policy, without breaking existing behaviour.
non_guessable: decision lives in git history (a documented commit), broken by a misleading 'perf' regression commit; git log/blame is the shortcut
decision_subject: fix: prorate the included quota and bill overage in blocks past the grace allowance
decision_rationale: Both support escalations traced to overage_charge ignoring the billing policy. The included quota prorates by calendar day: allowed so far is plan quota * day_of_month / days_in_month, rounded UP to the next whole unit - always ceil, never truncation, so a fractional day's unit counts in the customer's favor and nobody is billed off a rounding artifact. Only usage beyond that prorated allowance is overage. The first 25 overage units in the month are a free grace allowance, applied BEFORE any block rounding (billable = overage - 25, floored at zero) - that was the concession after the March billing-support incident, so trivial overruns never reach an invoice. What remains bills in 50-unit blocks, rounded UP to a whole block (a partial block bills as a full block) at plan['block_fee'] per block - never per unit, per-unit line items are what made reconciliation impossible.
